summary: Interleaved optimizer gatekeeper triggered high-p99 latency after tenant applied mixed batch/cache/quant profile
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sharp increase in p99 and tail token latency for a dedicated tenant after applying a new mixed optimizer profile that enables aggressive batching, prefix-KV prefetch, and a 4-bit quantization profile. Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible p99 tail latency spikes from ~220ms to 1.2s for streaming calls.
- Elevated token error retries and occasional 502s from the serving runtime during peak traffic windows.
- Customer-visible degradation affecting two critical inference pipelines (chat and classification).
Environment:
- Veloria Labs dedicated pool in prod/us-east, reserved capacity (dedicated), tenant ID veloria-774.
- Optimizer profile name: veloria-aggressor-v2 (applied 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC).
- Traffic: steady 560 rps with 5–20 token prompts typical.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Tenant toggled optimizer profile veloria-aggressor-v2 via Console rollout on 2026-03-09.
2) Observe streaming responses: increased end-to-end p99 in telemetry.
3) Compare serving-runtime traces pre/post profile change.
Logs / traces:
- Sampling of traces: link to Sentry traces and X-Ray segment IDs included in investigation notes.
- Metric highlights: sudden rise in serve_queue_time and kv-prefetch stall counts.
Workaround requested by customer:
- Immediate rollback to previous optimizer profile or apply a soft-gating stepdown to reduce batch sizes to baseline values.
- Request for a step-by-step rollback script we can run on their behalf with minimal disruption.
Desired outcome:
- Restore latency to baseline (<350ms p99) and verify no inference accuracy regression after rollback.
- Provide clear guidance and an automated, safe rollback path for mixed optimizations.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Maya Patel (Customer): Notified support: after enabling the new optimizer profile p99 jumped significantly. We can revert if you provide a step-by-step. We rely on steady low latency for our chat flows.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Support (Liam Chen): Acknowledged. Collecting traces and metrics from impacted pool. Can you confirm if you saw an increase in 502 errors or only latency?
2026-03-10 10:08 - Maya Patel (Customer): We saw a handful of 502s correlated with the highest traffic minute. Mostly latency otherwise.

2026-03-10 11:45 - Support (Liam Chen): Initial hypothesis: aggressive batching combined with KV prefetch is creating head-of-line stalls when quantized kernels fall back to slower paths. Opening INT ticket for runtime sampling.

2026-03-11 02:20 - SRE (Ana Rodriguez): Confirmed elevated kv-prefetch stall_count and a small percentage of model invocations hit a fallback observer that forces FP16 kernel on a subset of sequences. Dumped detailed traces to /artifacts/SUP-58139/trace-dump-20260311.zip

2026-03-11 08:30 - ENG (Tobias Weber): Noted a PR that adjusted kernel selection thresholds last week; possible interaction. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821. Recommend staged rollback: 1) disable kv-prefetch per-tenant 2) reduce max_batch_size 3) restore quant profile to previous baseline.
2026-03-11 12:05 - Support (Liam Chen): Shared an automated rollback playbook with customer for dry-run in staging. Customer requested we execute in prod after validation window.
investigation_notes: Metric analysis: p99 and p999 correlates with spikes in serve_queue_time. Batch sizes during spikes rose above expected due to burst policy combined with aggressive autoscaler thresholds.
Trace inspection: sequences that hit fallback kernels show higher memory pressure and KV cache misses leading to extra round trips to disk-backed cache in the dedicated pool image.
Repro step in staging: Reapplying veloria-aggressor-v2 in a staging replica reproduced tail latency within 30 minutes; disabling kv-prefetch eliminated most of the tail.

Hypothesis: Interaction between 4-bit quant profile and newest kernel-selection change produces non-deterministic fallback for sequences with long context and aggressive batching, increasing latency and 502s under load.

Risk assessment: Full immediate revert of quant profile may increase token cost and minor throughput regression but will likely restore latency SLA. Selective disable of kv-prefetch is lower risk and preserves most cost benefits.
resolution: Workaround applied 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC: Disabled per-tenant kv-prefetch flag and reduced max_batch_size from 64 to 32 for veloria-774. Result: p99 dropped to ~310ms within 20 minutes; 502s ceased. Next steps: schedule a staged reintroduction of quant profile with conservative kernel-selection thresholds and enable detailed telemetry on fallback events. Owner: Liam Chen. Follow-up ENG action: revert or adjust kernel-selection PR if further occurrences found.
